answer: Bonded sponsorship: a new agent may only join when an established sponsor locks a bond behind it, and that bond is slashed if the newcomer turns out to be fake. The sponsor's reputation flows like a river — one bad referral poisons the whole stream, so sponsors vet carefully. A hollow identity with no sponsor behind it simply cannot enter, and each sponsorship is checked through a prism of past behavior: repeat offenders lose the right to sponsor at all. A farm would need a thousand honest sponsors, not a thousand fake names.
